summary: Feed s128_double is degraded: required VLAN 20 is missing (50% untagged) and encrypted traffic at 93.9% exceeds NDR 90% tolerance. NDR needs both VLANs and full payload for detection.

findings.root_cause: Packet broker/TAP aggregation is stripping 802.1Q tags or forwarding from access ports as untagged. 50% of packets arrive untagged and VLAN 20 is never seen, indicating trunk tags are removed upstream or VLAN 20 not forwarded to this tool port.
findings.impact_on_tool: NDR requires VLANs 10 and 20 for segmentation-aware detection. Without VLAN 20 tags it cannot attribute traffic to the correct segment, missing lateral movement, segmentation violations and VLAN-specific policies - effectively blind to VLAN 20.

recommended_fix.why: Preserving 802.1Q tags and ensuring the broker forwards trunk traffic for VLANs 10 and 20 restores visibility so the NDR can correlate and detect per-VLAN threats.

findings.root_cause: 93.9% of bytes are encrypted (TLS), above the NDR's 90% tolerance. Traffic is predominantly TLS 1.2/1.3 with no upstream decryption, so the NDR receives only headers and encrypted payloads.
findings.impact_on_tool: NDR needs full payload for deep inspection. At this encryption level it is limited to metadata/flow analysis and cannot detect payload-based C2, exfiltration, or exploits inside encrypted sessions, reducing detection coverage.

recommended_fix.why: Selective decryption via a packet broker-integrated SSL visibility solution or feeding a decrypted copy will bring encrypted share below 90% and restore payload inspection without overwhelming the NDR.
